- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending down.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If model forecast mean is significantly higher than 30-day moving average of true prices, apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extreme deviations using 7-day rolling average of true prices as anchor.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often underperforms; increase forecast baseline by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
